## About This Project

This site organizes materials related to my LIS 4901 capstone project, *Cognitive Warrant: A Theoretical Framework for Evaluating Semantic Alignment in Knowledge Organization Systems*, as part of my requirements for the Master of Library and Information Science (MLIS) degree at the University of Denver.

The project investigates whether the categorical and hierarchical structures of the Library of Congress Subject Headings (LCSH) 
correspond to measurable patterns in our semantic cognition. Substituting LCSH boundaries for dictionary-derived sense boundaries, the study replicates the primed sensibility judgment paradigm of Trott and Bergen (2023) and extends their hybrid meaning theory through a novel heading appropriateness rating paradigm.


>Knowledge organization systems do not merely describe the world -- they impose structure on how users encounter it.
>
>The purpose of this study is to develop and empirically evaluate the concept of cognitive warrant as a principle for knowledge organization, defined as the extent to which the categorical and structural distinctions encoded in a knowledge organization system correspond to observable patterns in human semantic processing.
>
>Cognitive warrant, therefore, becomes a falsifiable claim: that professionally imposed boundaries track psychologically meaningful partitions in semantic space.
>
>Cognitive warrant positions knowledge organization research to engage empirically with the semantic processing and cognitive structure of the users library discovery systems are designed to serve.


## Site Contents

| Section | Contents |
|---|---|
| [Research Document](pages/manuscript.qmd) | This document contains material from my larger cognitive warrant research project. (The LIS 4901 Capstone paper was a *very* distilled version of that document.) It is a deliberate editorial selection from the full architecture, retaining the experimental design, statistical analysis plan, and theoretical contributions most relevant to a psycholinguistics audience while condensing material whose primary audience is library and information science (I am currently organizing the LIS version). |
| [Presentation Materials](pages/presentation.qmd) | The slides and posters from my Capstone presentation to MLIS faculty. |
| [IRB Packet](pages/irb.qmd) | Complete IRB exempt certification application materials. |
| [Summary Documents](pages/summary-documents.qmd) | These are two documents I created to explain simply what my capstone project was trying to accomplish. They might be helpful for those without an LIS background.|
| [HLM Analysis](pages/hlm-analysis.qmd) | This was an assignment in my Hierarchical Linear Models (HLM) course, requiring students to critique an empirical research article that utilizes HLM. Naturally, I took this opportunity to better understand the methodology of Trott and Bergen (2023).|
| [Cognitive Warrant Analytic Pipeline](pages/cognitive-warrant-pipeline.qmd) | An executable, narrated walkthrough of my research document's Chapter 5 proof-of-concept analysis -- logistic regression, entropy, and cognitive information -- with all code visible for transparency and reproducibility. |
| [Grant Proposal](pages/grant-proposal.qmd) | This was the main assignment in my cognitive neuroscience graduate seminar -- a grant proposal for a hypothetical research project. This is where I first came across Trott and Bergen (2023), and the proposal is an attempt at validating their hybrid meaning theory with magnetoencephalography (MEG).|
